courses.title: General IT — Operator to Support Specialist
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Run the Gary Civic Tech Desk for ten weeks: accounts, disks, tickets, then an after-hours change window.
courses.lesson_excerpt: At the Gary Civic Tech Desk the machine in front of a patron is not a personality. It remembers (files), it calculates (apps), and it talks (network). Beginners freeze when a window disappears because they cannot name which of those three jobs failed. Ticket 4417 from the library kiosk is a remember-job failure: the essay lived in a browser temp store and the idle timer (1200 seconds) wiped the se
courses.worked_example: Idle policy 1200s = 20 minutes. Patron sat down at 14:02, last keystroke 14:07, return 14:28. Session is gone. Restore from the auto-save folder if present; do not disable the timer as your first move — the timer is a shared-kiosk control.
courses.assignment: Build the required folder tree for ticket 4417, write a four-line operator journal (remember / calculate / talk / what broke), and describe one restore method that is not Ctrl+Z. No patron PII.

courses.title: Computer Networking — Packets to Campus Edge
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Parse a crafted frame, run LPM, and prove a four-router town on paper then in code.
courses.lesson_excerpt: The WAIKE Packet Range is a table, a switch, and four Raspberry-class endpoints named Pier, Yard, Shed, and Roof. Nothing here is magic. A message that cannot fit in one frame is chopped. Ethernet carries 1500-ish bytes of payload because the local wire agreed to that, not because the Internet is polite.
courses.worked_example: A 2000-byte application buffer on a 1500 MTU path becomes at least two IP datagrams. Peel Ethernet first (ethertype 0x0800), then IP, then TCP.
courses.assignment: Draw the sticky-note stack for a TLS web fetch from Pier to a library cache. Label who reads each header. No vendor GUI screenshots required.

courses.title: Cybersecurity — Harbor SOC Foundations
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Triage a fixture SIEM, enforce RBAC on a bot, and detect a length lie in a toy parser.
courses.lesson_excerpt: Harbor SOC is a classroom security operations center for WAIKE. Confidentiality, integrity, and availability still run the place. The 2026-09-01 ISC2 CC outline renames the second domain toward governance and threads AI through all five. We prefer that upcoming outline. We do not copy ISC2 items.
courses.worked_example: A triage bot with sudo would violate least privilege for a non-human identity and would turn a prompt injection into root. Harbor policy: bots read, humans close.
courses.assignment: Write a one-page Harbor governance memo: CIA applied to the ticket-summarizer bot, one GRC owner, and one prohibited data class.

courses.title: Software Builder — ForgeDesk to Device Lab Deploy
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Merge a real conflict, ship a checkout API, and pin a digest on local Device Lab compose.
courses.lesson_excerpt: The WAIKE Software ForgeDesk is a two-person civic issue tracker for Device Lab checkouts. Ticket 8801 opens when a volunteer edits routes.py on feature/kiosk-hours while the desk lead edited the same function on main. A conflict is not a personality crisis. It is two hashes that claim the same lines. You will read both sides, keep the authz guard that main added, and keep the hours table that the
courses.worked_example: Parents A and B both touch def open_hours. A adds require_role('desk'). B adds HOURS={...}. Survivor must include both tokens.
courses.assignment: Write a conflict report for ticket 8801 naming both parents, survivor tokens, and one wrong resolution the lab must fail.

courses.title: Hardware Engineering + Embedded Prototyping — ForgeSense Node
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Compute a divider, budget real MPNs, run Zephyr on QEMU, then digitally diagnose a sagging 3V3 rail.
courses.lesson_excerpt: WAIKE Device Lab Hardware Studio opens with SPICE-class network analysis before any iron heats. PHYSICAL_PENDING covers soldering and instruments. Digitally you solve a series divider: R1=1k, R2=3k, Vin=12V → I=3mA, Vout=9V. The lab checks your arithmetic, not a screenshot of a GUI.
courses.assignment: Submit SPICE network JSON and show handwritten KCL at the mid node.

courses.title: Process Improvement + Project Management — Device Lab Flow
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Charter a real wait problem, run DMAIC on fixture data, and critique an AI plan without inventing outcomes.
courses.lesson_excerpt: Process Studio: Device Lab noon checkout wait baseline 15 minutes. Charter states problem, goal metric with baseline, in/out scope. fabricated_outcomes must be false — no invented community impact.
courses.worked_example: problem wait>15m; goal baseline 15m→8m; in_scope queue+staffing; out_scope new building; fabricated_outcomes false.
courses.assignment: Write charter JSON and a one-page sponsor brief without invented stats.

courses.title: AI/ML + Edge AI — EdgeForge Bench
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Run the Gary EdgeForge Bench for ten weeks: civic occupancy CSV → metrics → tiny net → quantized inference → redacted RAG.
courses.lesson_excerpt: The EdgeForge Bench in Gary is a rolling rack of three Coral-class USB accelerators and a battered ThinkPad that only sees the civic Wi-Fi. Week 1 is not 'learn Python.' It is naming columns so a sensor CSV becomes a matrix you can defend to a librarian. Ticket EF-2101 ships a 480-row occupancy CSV: timestamp_iso, zone_id, people_count, rssi_dbm. Beginners paste the file into a notebook and celebr
courses.worked_example: 480 rows × 0.80 = 384 train; 96 validation by time order (not shuffle).
courses.assignment: Write a four-line operator journal for EF-2101 naming columns, train_n, val_n, and why shuffle is forbidden. Submit lab_data_split JSON. No face IDs.

courses.title: Data Visualization + BI — Civic Metrics Studio
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Run Civic Metrics Studio for ten weeks: clean waits → SQL → stats → charts → KPI story → hashed portfolio dashboard.
courses.lesson_excerpt: The Civic Metrics Studio in Ghana/Gary partnership hours starts with a dirty CSV of desk tickets: ticket_id, opened_at, closed_at, zone, wait_min. Ticket CM-3102 has 5% null wait_min and two impossible negatives. Cleaning is not optional décor — dashboards that average negatives invent 'negative waits' for the mayor.
courses.worked_example: 200 rows, 10 nulls → null_rate=0.05; negatives dropped (not abs).
courses.assignment: Document drop vs impute choice for CM-3102; submit lab_clean_nulls.

courses.title: Cloud + DevOps — ForgeCloud Platform
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Run ForgeCloud Platform for ten weeks: Linux perms → git → containers → CI → IAM/secrets → SLO → rollback → k8s probes → incident runbook.
courses.lesson_excerpt: ForgeCloud Platform starts on a Linux bastion that deploys nothing until permissions make sense. Ticket FC-4101 shows a deploy key file mode 0666 — world writable. You will compute the correct mode 0600 and refuse to continue CI until the lab's mode check passes. Cloud YAML cannot save a secret that every login can rewrite.
courses.assignment: Submit lab_linux_perms with mode_octal=384 (0600) and rationale.

courses.title: Wireless / 5G-Advanced / NTN / AI-RAN — Pier Radio Bench
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Run the Gary Pier Radio Bench for ten weeks: FSPL → OFDM → 5G-Advanced → NTN LEO delay → AI-RAN gated policy. Commercial standardized 6G does NOT exist today.
courses.lesson_excerpt:
The Pier Radio Bench sits under the Gary pier canopy: a USRP-class SDR, a scratched
ThinkPad, and a laminated card that says COMMERCIAL_STANDARDIZED_6G=false. Week 1 is
ticket WR-4101. Beginners want a 6G slide deck. Operators compute free-space path loss
for a 3.5 GHz pier hop at 120 m using FSPL_dB = 20*log10(d_m) + 20*log10(f_MHz) - 27.55.
courses.assignment: Journal WR-4101 with d_m, f_mhz, fspl_db, and commercial-6G=false. Submit lab_fspl_budget.

courses.title: Robotics and Control — HarborBot Bay
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Ten weeks in HarborBot Bay: frames → 2R kinematics → PID → traj → sensing → E-stop → diff-drive → estimation → message schemas → safety capstone. Real commands on fixture math.
courses.lesson_excerpt:
HarborBot Bay ticket RB-5101: a diff-drive cart on taped pier coordinates. Pose is (x,y,theta)
in meters/radians. Students compute a planar transform of a tool point and refuse 'AI nabbed
the box' stories without a frame diagram.
courses.worked_example: theta=π/2, tool offset (0.2,0) → tool maps to pier axes with sin/cos.
courses.assignment: Compute RB-5101 pose/tool map. Submit lab_se2_pose.

courses.title: Game Development — Forge Arcade Studio
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Ten Forge Arcade weeks: game loop → AABB → audio clock → entities → levels → input → optional four-game case studies → playtest metrics → a11y → ship checklist. Case studies are optional; not dependent on unmerged game branches.
courses.lesson_excerpt:
Ticket GA-6101: fixed timestep dt=1/60 with accumulator pattern. Lab checks dt, steps,
spiral_of_death_guard=true when frame_time exceeds 0.25 s clamp. Variable rendering may
interpolate; simulation steps stay fixed.
courses.assignment: Implement GA-6101 loop JSON. Submit lab_game_loop.
